grants.title: Municipal Permitting Modernization Program (PON 5862)
grants.description: $7.5 million available. Provides NYS municipalities (cities, towns, villages, counties) two years of no-cost access to Citizenserve, a software platform for building permitting, planning/zoning, code enforcement, and licensing. First-come, first-served; closes when funds are exhausted or by the deadline, whichever comes first.

grants.title: Charge Ready NY 2.0 (PON 5367)
grants.description: $12 million available. Incentives for installing Level 2 EV charging equipment at workplaces and multi-unit dwellings — $3,000 per port ($4,000 in Disadvantaged Communities). Municipalities, school districts, and other local government entities are eligible Equipment Owners. First-come, first-served; closes when funds are exhausted or by the deadline, whichever comes first.

grants.title: Charge Ready NY – Large Public Sector Project Program (PON 6141)
grants.description: $35 million available ($1M–$15M per award). Competitive proposal program for public sector and government entities to develop large portfolios of public Level 2 EV charging sites. Requires minimum 20% cost share. Unlike the other Charge Ready programs, this is a competitive proposal with a hard deadline, not first-come-first-served.

grants.title: Plus One ADU Program (Round 4)
grants.description: $12 million available. Grants to units of local government or non-profit housing organizations to administer local Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) creation/improvement programs for low- and moderate-income homeowners. Up to $125,000/unit ($175,000 in NYC). Applications are actually accepted on a rolling basis until funds are committed — 09/03/2026 is the priority-consideration cutoff, not a hard close, shown here as the practical deadline for now. Update this entry when a later round replaces Round 4.

grants.title: CDBG Housing (2026)
grants.description: Federal CDBG funding for eligible housing activities benefiting low- and moderate-income households, for cities/towns/villages under 50,000 population and counties under 200,000.

grants.title: CDBG Open Round (2026)
grants.description: Federal CDBG funding for Public Facilities (up to $1 million), Community Planning, Microenterprise Assistance, Stand-Alone Business Assistance, and Imminent Threat activities. Subject to availability of funds.

grants.title: CDBG Public Infrastructure (2026)
grants.description: 2026 CFA Public Infrastructure funding round is closed. Contact the Office of Community Renewal for technical assistance on future rounds.

grants.title: Affordable Housing Corporation – AHOD Program (2026-2027)
grants.description: Grants up to $75,000/unit for construction, acquisition/rehabilitation, or improvement of 1-4 family owner-occupied housing. Eligible applicants: municipalities (including municipal housing authorities and HDFCs) and qualifying not-for-profits. NOFA/RFP jointly released 07/16/2026 for the 2026-2027 round; accepted until AHC's appropriated funds are exhausted — no fixed closing date given. Covers three RFP tracks: Acquisition & Rehabilitation, Home Improvement, and New Construction.

grants.title: RESTORE Program (2026)
grants.description: $4 million available. Grants to units of local government and not-for-profits (1+ year serving the community) to act as Local Program Administrators providing emergency repair grants (up to $20,000/building) to homeowners age 60+ whose homes have hazardous conditions. Firm deadline — late applications are rejected outright, not just deprioritized.
